# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

timed() { local start=$SECONDS; "$@"; local rc=$?; printf '[timing] %s: %ss\n' "$1" "$((SECONDS-start))" >&2; return "$rc"; }
work="$RUNNER_TEMP/omgithub-v2"
script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
session="$(cat "$work/session-id")"
[[ "$session" == ses_* ]] || { echo 'Missing V2 session ID' >&2; exit 1; }
port="${V2_WEB_PROXY_PORT:-4097}"
upstream="http://127.0.0.1:${V2_SERVER_PORT:-4096}"
nohup node "$script_dir/v2-experiment-proxy.mjs" "$port" "$session" "$upstream" > "$work/proxy.log" 2>&1 &
echo "$!" > "$work/proxy.pid"
for _ in {1..30}; do
  code="$(curl --silent --max-time 2 --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' "http://127.0.0.1:$port/" || true)"

  sleep 1
done
[[ "${code:-}" == 200 ]] || { echo 'V2 proxy did not start' >&2; cat "$work/proxy.log" >&2; exit 1; }
asset=cloudflared-linux-amd64
if [[ "$RUNNER_OS" == macOS ]]; then
  asset=cloudflared-darwin-amd64
  [[ "$(uname -m)" == arm64 ]] && asset=cloudflared-darwin-arm64

if [[ "$asset" == *linux* ]]; then
  timed curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \

else

    --output "$work/cloudflared.tgz" "https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest/download/$asset.tgz"
  timed tar -xzf "$work/cloudflared.tgz" -C "$work" cloudflared
fi
chmod 755 "$work/cloudflared"
nohup "$work/cloudflared" tunnel --no-autoupdate --url "http://127.0.0.1:$port" > "$work/tunnel.log" 2>&1 &
echo "$!" > "$work/tunnel.pid"
origin=''
for _ in {1..60}; do
  origin="$(sed -nE 's#^.*\|?[[:space:]]*(https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com)[[:space:]]*\|.*$#\1#p' "$work/tunnel.log" | head -n 1)"
  [[ -n "$origin" ]] && break

done

url="$(node --input-type=module -e "import { v2SessionUrl } from '$script_dir/opencode-v2-api.mjs'; console.log(v2SessionUrl(process.argv[1], process.argv[2]))" "$origin" "$session")"

done

api="$(curl --silent --show-error --location --max-time 10 -u "opencode:$OPENCODE_PASSWORD" --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' "$origin/api/info" || true)"

Run `scripts/setup-linux-playwright.sh` on an Ubuntu worker to install the pinned

workflow run this before publishing SSH access. Use `playwright-cli` from Actions

Use `playwright-cli -s=check open <url>`, `eval`, `screenshot`, and `close` without
manual browser flags. Load `.github/templates/linux.md` by default. Select `mac.md` instead when

## Capture the Linux WebGPU triangle

Install Playwright 1.63.0 and its full Chromium browser as below. Install
`mesa-vulkan-drivers`, `vulkan-tools`, and `xvfb` on Ubuntu. Serve
`tests/fixtures/webgpu-triangle.html` over localhost HTTP. Run:

```sh
PLAYWRIGHT_ROOT=/tmp/gpu-runtime xvfb-run -a node scripts/gpu-capture.mjs \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/webgpu-triangle.html --canvas '#wgpu' \
  --backend swiftshader --require-green-triangle --out /tmp/linux-triangle
```

Keep the default Metal path for the Mac test.

```sh

```

Replace the URL and canvas selector with the running game's values. Start the

```
export function islandHeight(spec, x, z) {
  const R = spec.radius, H = spec.height, seed = spec.seed;
  const r = Math.hypot(x, z);
  const ang = Math.atan2(z, x);
  const cn = (fbm2(Math.cos(ang)*3.1 + seed, Math.sin(ang)*3.1 - seed*0.7, 3) - 0.5);
  const rr = r / R + cn * 0.055; // ±2.75%
  const falloff = smoothstep(1.02, 0.02, rr); // 1 center→0 at 1.02
  const ridge = ridged2(x*0.016 + seed*2.3, z*0.016 - seed*1.7, 4);
  const shape = 0.42 + 0.58*ridge;
  let h = H * falloff * shape;
  // hills detail
  h += (fbm2(x*0.045+seed, z*0.045-seed, 3) - 0.5) * H*0.16 * falloff;
  // shore terrace: flatten low elevations into wide beach
  const beach = smoothstep(0.0, 2.8, h); // 0 at waterline
  h = h * (0.55 + 0.45*beach); // reduce low slopes near shore? 
  h -= 2.0 * (1 - falloff) + 0.6;
  // micro detail
  h += (fbm2(x*0.22+seed*4, z*0.22-seed*4, 2)-0.5)*0.6*falloff;
  return h;
}
```

## Objective
- Build an open-world sailing exploration game from the user's terse Arabic prompt "🛥عالم مفتوح" (open world), with polished, AAA-quality visuals, mobile/touch support, day/night weather, islands, and treasure hunting.

## Requirements
- User gave no detailed requirements beyond "open world" with a boat emoji.
- Implicit repo expectation: static web game served from project root, mobile responsive with usable touch controls, playable in-browser, no external asset/network dependency at runtime.
- UI is Arabic-first (RTL) with bilingual accent labels.
- Capture automation auto-clicks a visible button whose text/aria-label is exactly `Start` or `Play`; current button uses `aria-label="Start"`.

## Decisions
- Built a Three.js + Vite static game (procedural everything: terrain, waves, ship, palms, audio) with Arabic UI using locally vendored Amiri/Cairo fonts.
- 8 handcrafted procedural islands with names/types: lighthouse home island, coral, falcons cliffs, old harbor ruins, mist volcano, palms, stars stone circle, sun cliffs.
- Gameplay: sail with W/S/A/D or joystick, anchor Space, interact E; discover islands, open shore chests, collect floating salvage, gold rewards, storm/day-night cycle, minimap/compass, victory condition.
- Software renderer detection disables shadow maps for SwiftShader; shadow maps otherwise enabled.
- No post-processing; uses procedural sky shader, Gerstner-style ocean shader, additive glow sprites, particle pools.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffolding (`package.json`, `index.html`, `src/style.css`, all game modules) and successful `npm run build`.
- Local server running on port 3002 (background PID saved at `/tmp/opencode/server.pid`).
- Playwright Chromium installed and headless/headed capture attempted; page now loads with **0 console errors** after fixing missing `buildCabin` call and merge-geometry errors.
- Title screen and initial gameplay screenshots captured to `screenshots/title.png`, `title2.png`, `game1.png`.
- Fixed: palm geometry merge, gull flight heading, favicon 404.
- Visual review identified concrete issues; fixes not yet applied.

### Active
- Visual/UX polish iteration based on screenshot feedback.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Fix HUD gold corruption: `this.gold` is a `ParticleField` in `Game.buildWorld`, overwriting/conflicting with `game.gold` state lookup in `UI.update`; rename particle field to `this.goldBurst` and update all refs (otherwise gold chip renders `[object Object]`).
2. Fix title typography: gold `em` renders as huge hollow outline; replace gradient/background-clip/filter styling with solid gold color, simplify title layout, verify Arabic shaping/contrast at 1440×900 and 390×844.
3. Move sun to front-left so island/sea/sails are lit and sun is visible: change `sunDirection()` azimuth offset (currently sun ends up behind camera); desired azimuth ≈210° at start time 17.15.
4. Set initial wind favorable: `state.windAngle` and `windTargetAngle` ≈ `Math.PI + 0.3` (currently 0.8 rad → upwind, ship only 1.3 knots).
5. Camera framing: offset default `orbitYaw` ≈0.28–0.35, distance ≈30–33, auto-recenter to that offset instead of 0 so the mast/sail doesn't hide the island/lighthouse.
6. Water look: brighter turquoise deep/shallow colors, reduce excessive crest foam/sparkle/“snow” streaks, soften island foam ring opacity.
7. Island detail: increase palm/bush/rock density and palm scale, add fake blob contact shadows (since SwiftShader capture has shadows off), add terrain ruggedness/color variation; beach currently reads as a flat beige shelf.
8. Ship visual: sails too pale/flat and jib oversized; improve contrast, reduce jib, ensure hull/deck detail reads; add contact shadow ellipse under hull.
9. Compass cleanup: remove duplicate `N` cardinal + `N 000` readout; simplify to one heading readout.
10. Re-capture desktop and mobile screenshots via `playwright-cli` and iterate; verify `CAPTURE_STRICT`-style no console/page errors and no HTTP 404s.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: game orchestration, lighting/weather, camera, input, salvage, rain, discovery/chest logic, debug `window.__voyage`.
- `src/style.css`: all HUD/title/responsive styling; title gradient issue here.
- `src/islands.js`: procedural island terrain/props/lighthouse/dock/ruins/chest/atmosphere.
- `src/terrain.js`: pure height/color/waterline functions and `ISLAND_SPECS`.
- `src/ship.js`: parametric hull, sails, mast, rigging, buoyancy, lantern.
- `src/ocean.js`: polar ocean grid + shader, CPU `heightAt`.
- `src/sky.js`: sky shader, palettes, `sunDirection`.
- `src/ui.js`: compass/minimap/wind canvases, toasts, HUD updates, victory.
- `src/wildlife.js`: gulls/dolphins.
- `src/effects.js`: particle fields and radial textures.
- `src/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio ambience/SFX.
- `src/noise.js`: noise/random/math helpers.
- `index.html`: HUD/title/victory markup; `Start` button has `aria-label="Start"`.
- `public/fonts/`: vendored Amiri/Cairo woff2 files.
- `screenshots/`: current captures (`title.png`, `title2.png`, `game1.png`).

## Important Context
- Server command: `PORT=3002 RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime node /home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/default-start.mjs`; it watches and rebuilds Vite.
- Playwright usage: `export DISPLAY=:0`, `playwright-cli -s=voyage open http://localhost:3002`, `reload`, `eval`, `screenshot --filename=screenshots/x.png`.
- Screenshot viewport is currently ~1050×793; capture harness uses 1440×900 desktop + 390×844 mobile.
- `this.gold` conflict is the known gold-chip bug; `UI.update` sets `textContent = game.gold` expecting a number.
- Software rendering is detected as SwiftShader/llvmpipe; shadows are intentionally disabled there, so visual depth must come from lighting, vertex colors, and fake contact shadows.
- Title screenshot shows sun behind camera (flat gray scene), huge hollow-gold “مفتوح”, dim subtitle, and sail centered blocking lighthouse.
- Gameplay screenshot shows `[object Object]` gold chip, sail blocking island, 1.3 knots due to unfavorable wind, overly white water foam, sparse vegetation, and flat lighting.
- `npm run build` currently succeeds; warnings only: chunk >500 kB and deprecated `THREE.Clock`.
- Changes are uncommitted.

263: function buildMainsailGeometry() {
264:   const S = 14
265:   const T = 18
266:   const positions = []
267:   const uvs = []
268:   const indices = []
269:   const topY = 12.4
270:   const span = 7.4
271:   for (let j = 0; j <= T; j++) {
272:     const v = j / T
273:     for (let i = 0; i <= S; i++) {
274:       const u = i / S
275:       const z = -(u * span * (1 - 0.8 * v) + 0.18)
276:       const y = v * topY + Math.sin(v * Math.PI) * 0.22
277:       const billow = Math.sin(Math.PI * Math.min(1, u * 1.02)) * Math.sin(Math.PI * v * 0.92) * (0.95 - v * 0.42)
278:       const x = -billow + 0.03
279:       positions.push(x, y, z)
280:       uvs.push(u, v)
281:     }
282:   }
283:   for (let j = 0; j < T; j++) {
284:     for (let i = 0; i < S; i++) {
285:       const a = j * (S + 1) + i
286:       const b = a + 1
287:       const c = a + (S + 1)
288:       const d = c + 1
289:       indices.push(a, b, c, b, d, c)
290:     }
291:   }
292:   const geo = new THREE.BufferGeometry()
293:   geo.setAttribute('position', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(positions, 3))
294:   geo.setAttribute('uv', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(uvs, 2))
295:   geo.setIndex(indices)
296:   geo.computeVertexNormals()
297:   return geo
298: }

300: function buildJibGeometry() {
301:   const A = new THREE.Vector3(0, deckAt(1) + 0.55, 7.6)
302:   const B = new THREE.Vector3(0, deckAt(0.6) + 15.2, 1.7)
303:   const C = new THREE.Vector3(0, deckAt(0.6) + 3.4, 1.7)
304:   const S = 12
305:   const T = 16
306:   const positions = []
307:   const uvs = []
308:   const indices = []
309:   const luff = new THREE.Vector3()
310:   const leech = new THREE.Vector3()
311:   const p = new THREE.Vector3()
312:   for (let j = 0; j <= T; j++) {
313:     const v = j / T
314:     luff.copy(A).lerp(B, v)
315:     leech.copy(C).lerp(B, v)
316:     for (let i = 0; i <= S; i++) {
317:       const u = i / S
318:       p.copy(luff).lerp(leech, u)
319:       const billow = Math.sin(Math.PI * u) * Math.sin(Math.PI * v) * 0.95 * (0.45 + 0.55 * (1 - v))
320:       positions.push(p.x + billow, p.y + Math.sin(u * Math.PI) * 0.1, p.z)
321:       uvs.push(u, v)
322:     }
323:   }
324:   for (let j = 0; j < T; j++) {
325:     for (let i = 0; i < S; i++) {
326:       const a = j * (S + 1) + i
327:       const b = a + 1
328:       const c = a + (S + 1)
329:       const d = c + 1
330:       indices.push(a, b, c, b, d, c)
331:     }
332:   }
333:   const geo = new THREE.BufferGeometry()
334:   geo.setAttribute('position', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(positions, 3))
335:   geo.setAttribute('uv', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(uvs, 2))
336:   geo.setIndex(indices)
337:   geo.computeVertexNormals()
338:   return geo
339: }

341: function addCylinderBetween(group, a, b, radius, material, radial = 6) {
342:   const dir = new THREE.Vector3().subVectors(b, a)
343:   const len = dir.length()
344:   const geo = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(radius, radius, len, radial)
345:   const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geo, material)
346:   mesh.position.copy(a).add(b).multiplyScalar(0.5)
347:   mesh.quaternion.setFromUnitVectors(new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0), dir.normalize())
348:   group.add(mesh)
349:   return mesh
350: }

448:   sampleSpots(count, { minH, maxH, maxSlope, minR, maxR, avoid = [] }) {
449:     const rng = this.rng
450:     const spots = []
451:     let attempts = 0
452:     while (spots.length < count && attempts < count * 60) {
453:       attempts++
454:       const a = rng() * TAU
455:       const rr = Math.sqrt(rng()) * maxR
456:       if (rr < minR) continue
457:       const x = Math.cos(a) * rr * this.radius
458:       const z = Math.sin(a) * rr * this.radius
459:       const h = islandHeight(this.spec, x, z)
460:       if (h < minH || h > maxH) continue
461:       if (this.localSlope(x, z, 1.8) > maxSlope) continue
462:       let blocked = false
463:       for (const av of avoid) {
464:         if (Math.hypot(x - av.x, z - av.z) < av.r) { blocked = true; break }
465:       }
466:       if (!blocked) {
467:         for (const s of spots) {
468:           if (Math.hypot(x - s.x, z - s.z) < 3.4) { blocked = true; break }
469:         }
470:       }
471:       if (blocked) continue
472:       spots.push({ x, y: h, z, rot: rng() * TAU, scale: 0.8 + rng() * 0.5 })
473:     }
474:     return spots
475:   }

477:   addInstances(geo, mat, spots, minScale, maxScale, sink) {
478:     if (!spots.length) return null
479:     const mesh = new THREE.InstancedMesh(geo, mat, spots.length)
480:     const dummy = new THREE.Object3D()
481:     for (let i = 0; i < spots.length; i++) {
482:       const s = spots[i]
483:       const sc = lerp(minScale, maxScale, (s.scale - 0.8) / 0.5)
484:       dummy.position.set(s.x, s.y - sink, s.z)
485:       dummy.rotation.set(0, s.rot, 0)
486:       dummy.scale.set(sc, sc * (0.92 + (i % 5) * 0.035), sc)
487:       dummy.updateMatrix()
488:       mesh.setMatrixAt(i, dummy.matrix)
489:     }
490:     mesh.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true
491:     mesh.castShadow = true
492:     mesh.receiveShadow = true
493:     this.group.add(mesh)
494:     return mesh
495:   }

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

import { startForCapture } from './capture-start.mjs'
import captures from './wip-screenshots.cjs'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => {
      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

## Objective
- Build a polished open-world sailing exploration game from the user's terse prompt "🛥عالم مفتوح" (open world), then continue visual/UX polish after the user added "الكتروني" (electronic).

## Requirements
- No detailed requirements beyond "open world" + boat emoji; latest user word "الكتروني" is ambiguous (possibly meaning an electronic/digital game, or a cyberpunk/electronic aesthetic) and may need clarification.
- Static web game served from project root; mobile responsive with usable touch controls; playable in-browser; no runtime external asset/network dependency.
- UI Arabic-first RTL with bilingual accent labels.
- Capture automation auto-clicks a visible button whose text/aria-label is exactly `Start` or `Play`; current button uses `aria-label="Start"`.
- Capture harness screenshots at 1440×900 desktop and 390×844 mobile, 1s after auto-start; strict mode fails on console/page errors or same-origin HTTP ≥400.

## Decisions
- Three.js + Vite static game with procedural terrain, waves, ship, palms, audio; locally vendored Amiri/Cairo fonts.
- 8 procedural islands: lighthouse home, coral, falcon cliffs, old harbor ruins, mist volcano, palms, star stone circle, sun cliffs.
- Gameplay: sail with W/S/A/D or joystick, anchor Space, interact E; discover islands, shore chests, floating salvage, gold, storms/day-night, minimap/compass, victory condition.
- Software renderer detection (SwiftShader/llvmpipe) disables shadow maps and now activates low-quality mode: Lambert materials, reduced terrain/ocean segments, merged static geometry, 0.72 render scale.
- Title screen renders the 3D backdrop once, then pauses GL rendering until Start to keep the button responsive under slow software presentation.
- No post-processing; procedural sky, ocean shader, additive glow sprites, particle pools.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffolding and `npm run build` success.
- Fixed earlier runtime errors, palm merge, gull heading, favicon 404; zero console errors previously.
- Fixed gold HUD bug: renamed ParticleField to `this.goldBurst`; `UI.update` now reads `game.state.gold/discoveredCount/chestCount`.
- Improved title typography: removed broken gradient/background-clip gold `em`, now solid gold; smaller title, top-aligned layout, scrim, faster opacity-only rise animation.
- Adjusted sun azimuth (`sunDirection` offset now `-0.58`) so start sun is front-left.
- Initial wind favorable (`Math.PI + 0.3`), sail 0.5.
- Camera defaults: `orbitYaw 0.34`, `distance 33`, `pitch 0.3`; auto-recenter to 0.34; title camera distance 46.
- Ocean: brighter turquoise deep/shallow, reduced crest foam/sparkle/surf; island foam opacity reduced.
- Islands: increased palm/cypress/bush/rock density and palm scale; added instanced fake contact shadows; increased terrain ruggedness/color variation.
- Ship: darker cream sail texture/contrast, smaller jib, added water contact-shadow ellipse.
- Compass: removed duplicate numeric heading readout (kept cardinal ribbon).
- HUD chips: Arabic labels fixed to `من ٨ جزر` / `من ٨ كنوز`; mobile compass/quest/toasts repositioned (portrait compass 154px, quest 120px, toasts 204px).
- Added software low-quality path: `setLowQuality`, Lambert conversion, reduced island terrain segments (76), merged island statics, reduced ocean geometry (84×116).
- Optimized salvage from ~110 draws to 2 (one InstancedMesh crate + one Points glow pool).
- Optimized wildlife: merged gull bodies (3 draws/gull: body + 2 wings), merged dolphin bodies (1 draw/dolphin).
- Boot overlay now `pointer-events:none` when hidden; `hideBoot()` called after `updateWorld`.
- Performance improved from ~2.5s/frame to ~0.8–1.7s software frames; draw calls reduced 450→223; terrain/props island renders now much cheaper.

+  // The ship is a few dozen small meshes. On software renderers every draw call
+  // is expensive, so bake all rigid parts into one mesh per material while
+  // leaving the animated pieces (sail, jib, flag, lantern) untouched.
+  mergeStatics() {
+    this.tilt.updateMatrixWorld(true)
+    const inv = new THREE.Matrix4().copy(this.tilt.matrixWorld).invert()
+    const tmp = new THREE.Matrix4()
+    const excluded = new Set([this.jib, this.flag, this.lantern, this.lanternGlass, this.lanternGlow, this.sailPivot])
+    const groups = new Map()
+    const remove = []
+    this.tilt.traverse((obj) => {
+      if (!obj.isMesh || obj.isSprite || obj.isInstancedMesh) return
+      let p = obj
+      while (p && p !== this.tilt) {
+        if (excluded.has(p)) return
+        p = p.parent
+      }
+      const mat = obj.material
+      if (!mat || Array.isArray(mat) || mat.transparent) return
+      let entry = groups.get(mat.uuid)
+      if (!entry) {
+        entry = { mat, geos: [] }
+        groups.set(mat.uuid, entry)
+      }
+      const src = obj.geometry.index ? obj.geometry.toNonIndexed() : obj.geometry.clone()
+      if (!src.attributes.position || !src.attributes.normal) return
+      for (const name of Object.keys(src.attributes)) {
+        if (name !== 'position' && name !== 'normal' && name !== 'uv') src.deleteAttribute(name)
+      }
+      if (!src.attributes.uv) {
+        src.setAttribute('uv', new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Float32Array(src.attributes.position.count * 2), 2))
+      }
+      tmp.copy(inv).multiply(obj.matrixWorld)
+      src.applyMatrix4(tmp)
+      entry.geos.push(src)
+      remove.push(obj)
+    })
+    for (const { mat, geos } of groups.values()) {
+      if (!geos.length) continue
+      const merged = geos.length === 1 ? geos[0] : mergeGeometries(geos, false)
+      if (!merged) continue
+      const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(merged, mat)
+      mesh.castShadow = true
+      mesh.receiveShadow = true
+      this.tilt.add(mesh)
+    }
+    for (const obj of remove) obj.parent?.remove(obj)
+  }
